metrics.d1Help: % of players who return on day 2. Indicates whether the game made a good first impression. Problems here almost always lie in the tutorial or first session.
metrics.d3Help: % of players still active after 3 days. Signals whether the initial hook is keeping interest beyond the first return. A sharp drop from D1 to D3 indicates the secondary loop hasn't engaged yet.
metrics.d7Help: % of players still active after 7 days. Measures whether the core loop engages. A sharp drop from D1 to D7 usually means the loop doesn't hook players.
metrics.d14Help: % of players still active after 14 days. Mid-game marker: if D7 was ok but D14 drops, the game loses momentum before the long-term content.
metrics.d30Help: % of players still active after 30 days. Reflects whether the mid-game has enough depth to maintain long-term interest.
metrics.sessionsHelp: How many times per day the average player opens the game. High values indicate good compulsiveness and return hooks (notifications, energy, events).
metrics.durationHelp: Average session length in minutes. Too short may indicate frustrating sessions or scarce content. Too long may tire the player.
metrics.conversionHelp: % of players who made at least one purchase (currency, skin, battle pass...). It's the primary health indicator for game monetization.

diag.fillHint: Fill in D1, D7 or D30 above to see the diagnosis.

withTutorial.headline: Tutorial breaking
withTutorial.detail: Player isn't even reaching D7. They're probably leaving before feeling the fun of the game.
tips: Shorten the tutorial — the ideal is under 3 minutes
Give a satisfying reward before the tutorial ends
Show the core loop in the first session, no delays
Remove entry barriers: no wait times in the first 10 minutes
Let the player fail and recover — don't block progress on failure

noTutorial.headline: First session doesn't convince
noTutorial.detail: Without a formal tutorial, the player doesn't understand what to do right away and leaves early.
tips: Without a formal tutorial, the first session must be self-explanatory
Get the player doing something satisfying in the first 60 seconds
Use contextual UI hints to guide without interrupting
Give a clear reward after the first successful action
Test with someone who's never seen the game — watch where they get stuck

default.headline: Loop doesn't hook
default.detail: Player arrives on D1 but doesn't come back. There's no concrete reason to open the game on D2, D3...
tips: Add a pending reward that can only be collected the next day
Create a short-term goal that doesn't end in the first session
Push notification on D1 with something concrete waiting for the player
Review the core loop — is it clear what to do next?
The level difficulty curve should be gentle in the first 10 levels

pvp.headline: PvP doesn't maintain engagement between matches
pvp.detail: Player arrives on D1 but doesn't come back. There's no concrete reason to open the game on D2, D3...
tips: Add a pending reward that can only be collected the next day
Create a short-term goal that doesn't end in the first session
Push notification on D1 with something concrete waiting for the player
PvP loop needs visible progression even in defeat (XP, ranking, shards)
Check matchmaking — excessive imbalance destroys retention
Each match should end with a perceptible gain (skin, currency, progress)

sandbox.headline: Directionless sandbox loses players fast
sandbox.detail: Player arrives on D1 but doesn't come back. There's no concrete reason to open the game on D2, D3...
tips: Add a pending reward that can only be collected the next day
Create a short-term goal that doesn't end in the first session
Push notification on D1 with something concrete waiting for the player
In sandbox, the initial loop should show possibilities, not obligations
Offer a suggested (not forced) goal to guide the first few days
Social structure (seeing others' creations) creates powerful external motivation

progression.headline: Loop doesn't hook
progression.detail: Player arrives on D1 but doesn't come back. There's no concrete reason to open the game on D2, D3...
tips: Add a pending reward that can only be collected the next day
Create a short-term goal that doesn't end in the first session
Push notification on D1 with something concrete waiting for the player
The progression curve should have satisfaction peaks every 2–3 sessions
Let players perceive their evolution through visual comparisons (before/after)
Content unlocks are more motivating than pure number increases

default.headline: Empty mid-game
default.detail: Player runs out of things to do around the mid levels. Long-term retention is dropping.
tips: Check if there are medium-term goals — building targets, collections, progression
Social features (friends, guilds) create external motivation loops
Seasonal events or new content keep veteran players engaged
Review difficulty progression — is it blocked by a paywall?

pvp.headline: Empty mid-game
pvp.detail: Player runs out of things to do around the mid levels. Long-term retention is dropping.
tips: A league or season with exclusive rewards creates long-term urgency
Clans and guilds create social commitment that keeps players in the mid-game
Seasonal events or new content keep veteran players engaged
Review difficulty progression — is it blocked by a paywall?

default.headline: Weak monetization
default.detail: Good retention, but players aren't converting to paying customers.
tips: Review offer triggers — do they appear at a moment of frustration or desire?
The first offer (starter pack) needs to feel like an incredible deal
Test lower prices with more frequency vs high price and rare
Check if there are clear pain points without a reasonable free solution

ads.headline: Low engagement affects ad revenue
ads.detail: With a session-based model, game frequency and duration are your main revenue indicator.
tips: With an ads model, focus should be on frequent sessions and high average duration
Rewarded ads (watch to earn) have much higher acceptance than forced banners
Limit interstitial frequency — too many ads destroy retention
Offer an ad-removal option as the sole IAP — it converts well

premium.headline: Engagement below expectations
premium.detail: With a session-based model, game frequency and duration are your main revenue indicator.
tips: Premium games have no recurring conversion — focus on reviews and word of mouth
DLCs and expansions are the main vector for additional revenue
High retention generates positive reviews that fuel organic acquisition

ads.headline: Low engagement affects ad revenue
ads.detail: With a session-based model, game frequency and duration are your main revenue indicator.
tips: With an ads model, focus should be on frequent sessions and high average duration
Rewarded ads have much higher acceptance than forced banners
Limit interstitial frequency — too many ads destroy retention
Offer an ad-removal option as the sole IAP — it converts well

default.headline: Engagement below expectations
default.detail: With a session-based model, game frequency and duration are your main revenue indicator.
tips: Review daily return hooks (energy, rewards, notifications)
The session curve should have a clear natural stopping point (not frustration)
Test shorter, more frequent sessions vs long and rare sessions

great.headline: Healthy numbers
great.detail: Your game is within or above the benchmark for this genre. Keep monitoring.
tips: Keep the weekly analysis rhythm even when things are going well
Time to think about expansion — new acquisition channels or engagement features

funnel.howToUseText: You need to map where your funnel breaks. Below is the industry standard for {genre} — compare and identify where you fall short.

d1: Long or boring tutorial before feeling the loop
Wait times too early (crops take hours)
No clear reward in the first session
d7d30: Lack of medium-term goal (e.g.: building something big)
Repetitive loop with no novelty after level 15
Absence of seasonal events or content

d1: Overly restrictive tutorial — player wants to play immediately
First level too easy and dull
d7d30: Lack of new mechanics after the first 20 levels
Difficulty spikes block the player without explanation
No streak or visible daily reward

d1: Long cutscene or intro before action
Confusing stats system for non-genre players
d7d30: Lack of ongoing narrative to engage
Guild / social absent in the early phase

d1: First levels too easy — no challenge or satisfaction
Core mechanic not explained with visual clarity
d7d30: Lack of mechanic variation after a few levels

routine.title: Weekly data routine
routine.subtitle: Consistency beats talent. These weekly time blocks are enough to make good product decisions.
routine.footer: These times are estimates for small teams. With more data and automation (dashboards, alerts), the daily check can drop to 2 minutes.

rows.task: Open analytics, check previous day's D1, sessions/day and churn by level. If something is out of pattern, note it for investigation.
Deep review: D1/D7/D30 curve by weekly cohort. Compare with the previous week.
Check active A/B tests. Is there statistical significance? Continue, end or adjust?
Raise hypotheses for the weekly report. Build the narrative: what changed, why, what to test.
Write weekly report: numbers → hypotheses → learnings → next experiments.

questions.whyText: Data without questions is just numbers. These questions turn KPIs into product actions.
questions.footer: Remember to log each week's learning here in the "Main KPIs" tab — the decision history is more valuable than any dashboard.

retention.a: Problem in the tutorial or first session. Player didn't feel the fun before leaving.

retention.q: D7 drops a lot compared to D1?
retention.a: Short-term loop isn't retaining. Missing goals to bring the player back on day 2 and 3.
Empty mid-game. Ran out of things to do between levels 20 and 50.

retention.q: Which level has the most churn?
retention.a: That's your priority intervention point. Could be a difficulty spike or a content void.

experiments.q: What did we test this week?
experiments.a: Always 1 active hypothesis. Never test everything at once — you won't know what worked.
Yes → implement. No → discard or reformulate. Inconclusive → more data or clearer hypothesis.
This is the real value of the weekly report. Without recorded learning, you'll repeat the same mistakes.
Always leave with at least 1 defined experiment. Without an active hypothesis, the week is lost.
